chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, who said:

A man mentioned his wife to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), praising her well. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Have you made her jealous (with ghayrah)?' He said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So make her feel jealous.' So he made her feel jealous, and she remained steadfast (in her loyalty). So he said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have made her feel jealous, and she remained steadfast.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'She is as you say.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَغَرْتَهَا: Have you made her jealous (with ghayrah)?

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on inducing jealousy in a spouse for loyalty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia scholarly understanding of 'ghayrah' not merely as possessive jealousy, but as a virtuous protective instinct that safeguards marital fidelity. The Imam’s instruction to 'induce' this trait highlights the dynamic interplay between husband and wife, where the man’s encouragement fosters the woman’s steadfastness in maintaining her honor. The narrative concludes with the Imam’s validation of her character, emphasizing that a stable 'ghayrah' is a sign of moral integrity in the domestic sphere.
